findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 9 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints the codomain of the restricted function as (-\infty, 1) \cup (1, \infty). That set wrongly contains every number between -1 and 1 (which \csc x never takes) and leaves out -1 and 1 (which it does take: \csc\frac{\pi}{2} = 1, \csc\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1). The correct statement is f : \left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right] \to (-\infty, -1] \cup

Book correction: In this sentence the book writes (-\infty, -1) \cup (1, \infty) twice, with round brackets. The end points -1 and 1 belong to the set, so the brackets must be closed: (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty). There is also a stray colon in \to:, which should be just \to. Correctly: \csc^{-1} : (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty) \to \left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right]

Book correction: The book's caption under Figure 9.11(a) reads 'Graph of y = \csc x from -2\pi to 2\pi', copied from Figure 9.10. Figure 9.11(a) shows only the principal branch on \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]; our caption says this.
